name: SowTrack Conversion Tracking
author: SowTrack

sections.description:
LeadSeed sets up Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager for small businesses, so they can see
which ads bring them leads. This plugin is how your WordPress site turns that tracking on.

  1. Install and activate this plugin.
  2. Tap Connect to LeadSeed (on the Plugins screen, or under LeadSeed in your WordPress
    menu), then tap Approve in LeadSeed. You land back in your LeadSeed setup, connected.
    Prefer a token? Open LeadSeed in your WordPress menu, choose “Have a connection token
    instead? Paste it”, paste the token from your LeadSeed onboarding (“Turn on tracking” step), and
    click Save & check connection.
  3. That’s it. The plugin fetches your Google Tag Manager container from LeadSeed and adds the
    snippet to every page for you. The settings page shows whether your connection is live, and
    Disconnect this site turns it off.

  • Adds your Google Tag Manager snippet to every page (in the <head>, plus the standard
sections.faq:
Do I need a LeadSeed account?

Yes. The plugin connects your site to LeadSeed; without an account it cannot add any tracking.
Sign up at https://myleadseed.com.

Do I need a connection token?

Not usually. Tap Connect to LeadSeed and approve in LeadSeed instead. If the button can’t
finish on your site (a security or caching plugin can block the link back), the plugin says so and
offers the paste box.

Where do I get the connection token?

From your LeadSeed onboarding, on the “Turn on tracking” step. It starts with ls_.

How do I disconnect my site?

Open LeadSeed in your WordPress menu and tap Disconnect this site. Tracking stops on your
pages straight away. If any leads haven’t reached your lead sheet yet, the page tells you how many
first: disconnecting deletes them from your site.

The settings page says leads are waiting to be sent.

Nothing to do: they are safe on your site and the plugin keeps trying until LeadSeed confirms each
one. If the number keeps growing for more than a day, or the page says leads could not be saved on
this site, check your LeadSeed connection or contact LeadSeed support.

It says “Token rejected”.

Re-copy the token from LeadSeed and paste it exactly (no extra spaces), then click Save & check
connection again. If you have lost the token, generate a new one in LeadSeed; the new one replaces
the old.

Does this edit my theme?

No. The snippet is added by the plugin when each page is built, so it survives theme updates.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating stops the snippet and the scheduled check straight away. Leads still waiting to be
sent stay saved and are sent after you reactivate it. Deleting the plugin also removes everything it
stored, including your connection token and any leads still waiting to be sent.
sections.changelog:
1.7.1

  • The LeadSeed settings page now shows which LeadSeed account the site is connected to: the
    account’s sign-in email address and, when there is one, its business name. Sites already connected
    show it after updating, without connecting again.
  • Reconnect now sends LeadSeed a one-way fingerprint of the site’s current connection token (never
    the token itself), so LeadSeed can warn you before moving the site to a different account.
  • Tracking, leads, Connect and Disconnect work exactly as before.

1.7.0

  • Renamed to SowTrack Conversion Tracking; no functional change. The plugin still connects your
    site to LeadSeed, and its LeadSeed menu, settings and connection are unchanged.
  • The plugin’s folder is now sowtrack.

1.6.0

  • Leads can now be delivered through LeadSeed, which writes them into the lead sheet in your own
    Google account — no Apps Script to paste or deploy. LeadSeed tells the plugin which way your
    account works; sites on the older Apps Script setup keep working exactly as before.
  • Every lead sent through LeadSeed is saved on your own site first and kept until LeadSeed confirms
    it, so a lead is never lost to a brief outage. Sending happens after the visitor’s page has
    finished, so forms are never slowed down.
  • The settings page shows how many leads are waiting to be sent, if any. Disconnecting tells you
    first if waiting leads would be deleted.
  • Opening your site through LeadSeed’s test link marks your own test enquiry as a test.

1.5.0

  • New Connect to LeadSeed button: tap it, approve in LeadSeed, and you’re connected. No token to
    copy. Your site and LeadSeed swap the connection token directly, server to server.
  • New Disconnect this site button on the LeadSeed settings page.
  • Until the site is connected, the Plugins screen shows a reminder to connect, which you can dismiss.
  • The paste-a-token form still works exactly as before. Sites already connected with a token stay
    connected when they update.

1.4.0

  • Prepared for the WordPress.org plugin directory: the plugin’s folder is now leadseed, scripts
    are printed with WordPress’s own script helpers, and the readme documents every external service
    the plugin uses.
  • Requires WordPress 5.7 or later.
  • If you installed an earlier version from a .zip file, deactivate and delete it before installing
    this one, then paste your connection token again (deleting the old copy removes its settings).
    While an older copy is still active, WordPress will refuse to activate this version.

1.3.0

  • Lead capture now also covers SureForms, Elementor Pro forms, Fluent Forms, Ninja Forms and
    Jetpack Forms — alongside Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms and WPForms. Same direct site-to-Google
    flow: your leads go straight to your own Google Sheet and are never routed through LeadSeed.
  • The connection status endpoint now reports whether a lead destination is configured, so LeadSeed
    support can tell “not connected yet” apart from “connected but not working” without asking you to
    dig through wp-admin. Only a yes/no is exposed — never your sheet URL or your secret.

1.2.0

  • Lead capture now also forwards WPForms submissions (Lite and Pro, AJAX and native) to your
    connected Google Sheet — same direct site-to-Google flow as Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms.

1.1.0

  • Lead capture: forwards Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms submissions (with ad click-IDs) straight
    to the Google Sheet you connect in LeadSeed. Lead data flows directly into that sheet — it is never
    routed through LeadSeed.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: pull-based GTM snippet injection + connection status endpoint.

short_description: Connects your site to LeadSeed, which sets up Google Tag Manager and conversion tracking for you. No theme editing; survives theme updates.
